film.title: Spring Forward: The Night Court Street Lost an Hour (Athens, Ohio, 1997)
film.description:
April 6, 1997. Athens, Ohio. The clocks spring forward, last call comes an hour early, and about a thousand people, mostly Ohio University students, fill North Court Street. About 70 officers move in. Trash cans burn, bottles fly, and four rounds of wooden pellets go into the crowd. Forty-seven people are arrested.

Nearly thirty years later, the real story isn't the fire. It's the inversion: what the generation that yelled at the police line on Court Street thinks about police lines now.

An animated film from Hardwood Bricks Productions, in association with JuiceboxNationTV Entertainment. A 19 North Films film. Written by Matthew Hagan. Narration is an AI voice. Cover art and some illustrations are AI-made; the figures are stylized and are not real people. Social posts shown are invented composites. Music and sound are original. Photographs of Court Street by Matthew Hagan.

Sources: College Press Service wire, April 1997; Joe Donatelli, "A look back at the Ohio University daylight saving time change not-riots of 1997-98" (2024), quoting The Post, Dean of Students Joel Rudy and Athens police; The New Political (2025); The Post, April 14, 1998. 2024 vote: exit polls and AP VoteCast via AARP; Pew Research Center validated voters. No public poll isolates Gen X men; the nearest groups are shown. The generational argument is commentary.

Keep it mid. Keep it real. See more at https://hardwoodbricks.com

reels.title: The night Court Street lost an hour
reels.text: April 6, 1997. Athens, Ohio. Daylight saving time cut last call short, and about a thousand people filled North Court Street.

reels.title: It was never authority we had a problem with
reels.text: Thirty years after the Court Street time-change night, a Gen X confession: it was responsibility we were raging against.
